description: INF (identity of min) is 2^32, which is smaller than values reachable after several range adds.
trigger: Many range-add updates pushing every element of a queried range above 2^32.

description: Applying an affine map to a node sums two reduced terms without a final % MOD, leaving values in [MOD, 2*MOD).
trigger: A query whose range is exactly one segment-tree node that was just updated and whose new sum lands in [MOD, 2*MOD).

description: Composition stores f.b + (f.a*x.b % MOD) into an int without the outer % MOD, so repeated composition overflows int.
trigger: Deep composition chains (larger n, many assigns) where unreduced constants exceed 2^31.

description: Query starts the running minimum at 1e9 (the max |a_i|), forgetting that linear adds can push all values higher.
trigger: Many positive linear adds so that every value in a queried range exceeds 1e9.

description: Special case for n == 1 prints the initial value and ignores range-affine updates.
trigger: n = 1 with at least one update before a point query.

description: Prefix popcounts of the bit vector use 32-bit popcount on 64-bit words, dropping the high half of each word.
trigger: n > 64 so that more than one word exists and the upper 32 bits of an earlier word contain ones.

description: Li Chao tree is filled with the dummy line y = 5e17, which is not larger than every real line value (up to 2e18).
trigger: Few lines, so the true minimum at a query point is above 5e17.

description: Short queries inside block 0 are not answered naively and go through the Mo path, which assumes R >= block end.
trigger: Several short queries (L and R in the first block).

description: When the back stack is rebuilt from the front stack, the moved half is not reversed, so composition order is wrong.
trigger: pop_back on an empty back stack while the front stack holds 2+ elements that get moved.

description: Fenwick add stops at i < n and never updates the last node.
trigger: A value with more than 64 occurrence slots (several blocks) whose full-prefix count is queried.

description: At equal x, points are processed before query corners, so points on a rectangle's left/right edge are counted wrongly.
trigger: A point whose x equals a query's l or r with y in [d, u).

description: Missing seaweeds are mapped to n + 1 instead of n, which needs one more bit than the wavelet matrix has when n = 2^k - 1.
trigger: n of the form 2^k - 1 (1, 3, 7, ...).

description: Manacher mirror step uses k+res[i-k] < j-1, so a mirrored palindrome ending one before the boundary is not extended.
trigger: A palindrome whose mirror ends exactly one position before the current palindrome's left boundary.

description: Best length starts at -1, so when no common character exists a length-0 answer with a nonzero start is printed.
trigger: S and T share no character (e.g. all 'a' vs all 'b'), likely only for short strings.

description: Answer formula counts h-values < b+1 instead of < b.
trigger: Any query where some h value equals b.

description: Letters are encoded from 0, so 'a' gets code 0 and behaves like the wildcard.
trigger: An alignment where 'a' faces a different letter.

description: Z-box reuse starts one past the mirrored value, skipping the mismatch check at r[i-j].
trigger: Periodic strings where a mismatch sits right after a mirrored match inside the Z-box.

description: SA-IS names the smallest LMS substring 0 instead of 1, colliding with the next name when equal LMS substrings follow.
trigger: Strings with 3+ LMS positions and repeated LMS substrings (longer, periodic strings).

description: SA-IS names the smallest LMS substring 0 instead of 1, giving a wrong suffix array and wrong LCP sum.
trigger: Strings with 3+ LMS positions and repeated LMS substrings (longer, periodic strings).

description: Duval scan stops one character early, so the last character is never compared.
trigger: Strings where the last character would extend or change the current Lyndon factor.

description: DFS skips up to two edges back to the parent, so a doubled tree edge is wrongly treated as a bridge.
trigger: Exactly two parallel edges between a vertex and its DFS parent with no other cycle.

description: Absorbing along the path uses in[u] < in[w], missing the case where the back edge lands exactly on u.
trigger: A back edge whose endpoint is the head of the current path.

description: Divide-and-conquer includes edge M in the left half's graph, so merges are dated one step early.
trigger: An edge whose index equals a split point and closes a cycle.

description: Edge orientation breaks degree ties by input order, so equal-degree triangles can be oriented cyclically and missed.
trigger: A triangle whose three vertices have equal degree.

description: Neighbour flags are never cleared, so later BFS steps treat stale neighbours as adjacent.
trigger: A component needing two or more BFS steps.

description: When popping the stack, the previous left child is not re-attached to its new parent.
trigger: Two or more consecutive pops when a smaller element arrives.

description: Point updates go to the Fenwick tree but not to a[], whose value is used for the LCA term.
trigger: A path query whose LCA was updated earlier.

description: Fenwick add uses i < n and never updates node n.
trigger: A subtree query whose Euler range ends at n (vertices on the rightmost DFS path).

description: NTT size is chosen for n+m-2 instead of n+m-1, so the convolution wraps when n+m-1 is 2^k+1.
trigger: Depth arrays of length >= 8 (NTT path) with 2*len-1 = 2^k + 1, i.e. deep trees.

description: HLD lca uses < instead of <=, so when one vertex is the head of the other's heavy path it climbs too far.
trigger: A query whose endpoints' lca is the head of a heavy path.
